change_summary: The journal retracted the paper after an institutional investigation found the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated. The paper's Figures 2 to 4 show n-back accuracy by dose, and the notice says the conclusions cannot be relied on. The authors have not responded.
evaluation: Your Introduction cites Brown and Kim [3] as showing that 200 mg of caffeine improves working memory by 12%, which is why you chose a 200 mg dose. The stored paper reports a 12% accuracy gain at 200 mg and says Figures 2 to 4 show accuracy by dose. The journal has retracted the article, and the notice says the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated and the conclusions cannot be relied on. This is the draft's only citation of the paper and it is the stated rationale for your dose, so the impact is high.
recommendation: The journal has retracted the article, and the notice says the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated and the conclusions cannot be relied on. Your Introduction cites Brown and Kim [3] as showing that 200 mg of caffeine improves working memory by 12%, which is why you chose a 200 mg dose. Remove or replace that citation and re-check the claim it supported. Find other support for the 200 mg dose rationale, or say it is not backed by published evidence.
